questions.stem: A probability value is always a number that sits…
questions.correctFeedback: 0 means never, 1 means certain, and everything possible lives in between.
questions.incorrectFeedback: It runs from 0 (never) to 1 (certain). Percentages like 70% are just 0.7 in disguise.

questions.stem: The "bag of every possible outcome" is properly called the…
questions.correctFeedback: The sample space is the full collection of everything that could happen — the whole bag.
questions.incorrectFeedback: That's the sample space. An outcome is one item in the bag; an event is a chosen group of them.

questions.stem: "The die shows an even number" is best described as an…
options: event — a yes/no question on outcomes
outcome — one single face, like four
sample space — all six faces together
axiom — a basic rule we agree
questions.correctFeedback: It's an event: a chosen bunch of outcomes ({2,4,6}) that answers a yes/no question.
questions.incorrectFeedback: It's an event — a group of outcomes ({2,4,6}). A single outcome would be just one face, like 'a 4'.

questions.stem: If the chance a train is late is 0.2, the chance it is on time is…
options: zero point two, the same value
one point two, by adding one
zero point five, a coin toss
zero point eight, one minus it
questions.correctFeedback: Late and on-time can't both happen and cover everything, so on-time = 1 − 0.2 = 0.8 (the complement rule).
questions.incorrectFeedback: On-time = 1 − 0.2 = 0.8. 'Late' and 'on time' are opposites that together must total 1.
